PullRequest.Title: Polish pinned session chat hierarchy connectors
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #332997

## Summary

- keep pinned/sticky session hierarchy guides aligned without shifting session content
- use continuous, rounded chat connectors with deliberate spacing before status icons
- use the higher-contrast tree guide token consistently to avoid visible shade changes
- normalize session chevron and phone-layout codicon sizing
- extend the existing component fixture to cover a pinned, sticky session with nested chats

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts --grep "hierarchy guides"`
- `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/media/sessionsList.css`
- editor diagnostics and `git diff --check`

Scenarios.Scenario: Render or scroll the sessions list with pinned/sticky sessions, including phone layout
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The tree renders a visible session row, applies existing reactive classes, then browser style/layout/paint produces the row. The changed CSS replaces an existing sticky border/padding treatment with one absolutely positioned pseudo-element and normalizes codicon font sizes; no new awaited work blocks the row.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cold visible rows trigger resolveChatSessionItem for lazy provider-backed session properties.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one resolve per cold session resource until the provider refresh clears _resolvedResources; repeated renders and warm rows reuse the guard and cached observable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same renderSession call and cold-resource resolve occurred before the diff; the CSS changes do not alter render frequency, resource keys, caching, or concurrency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The call is fire-and-forget and is not awaited by rendering, so the provider resolve is off the immediate row paint critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Browser work scales with currently rendered sticky rows, not total session history because the list renderer virtualizes rows. Each rendered sticky row now has one generated marker box; chat guide box count and renderer cardinality are unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: DOM class updates and style/layout/paint execute on the UI thread. Existing provider resolves may overlap asynchronously across distinct cold resources; the diff does not change this concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: AgentSessionsModel deduplicates cold resolves with _resolvedResources and caches per-resource observables; warm rerenders do not re-resolve unless a provider refresh deliberately clears the guard. CSS has no application cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the changed rendering mechanism and unchanged provider boundary based on the CSS selectors, renderer call path, and resolve guard.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact paint cost varies by browser and visible row count, but one simple absolutely positioned marker per sticky visible row replaces border/padding paint and is not a realistic actionable regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The small constant paint-box change preserves event cadence and effective row cardinality, while icon sizing changes only glyph geometry.

Scenarios.Scenario: Expand a session with nested chats and reveal hierarchy guides by hover or selection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Expansion creates existing chat row templates; hover/selection toggles session-hierarchy-guides-visible, followed by browser style recalculation and paint. The diff changes border color and connector geometry on the same existing ::before/::after boxes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Paint work scales with the rendered chat children of the active expanded session. The diff does not add pseudo-elements, selectors that traverse larger collections, or additional event handlers; it only reshapes the existing two guide boxes per chat row and the existing session guide.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Hover handling, class toggling, and browser paint are serialized on the UI thread; there is no new queue, fan-out, or asynchronous work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used or invalidated by the CSS change. Existing DOM templates are reused by the virtualized tree before and after the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the unchanged renderer class toggles and the before/after CSS pseudo-element structure.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser-specific border-radius paint cost is unmeasured, but the primitive count and affected rows are unchanged, making any delta negligible and non-actionable.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The connector changes retain the same O(rendered child rows) style and paint behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Generate the nested-chat component screenshot fixture with a pinned, sticky session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Fixture setup maps the supplied session specs, derives pinned and sticky mock state, constructs the in-memory SessionsList, clicks the pinned section, then waits one microtask before dispatching mouseover for screenshot capture.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The added filter/map/flatMap work is linear in the fixture's small, fixed sessions array and runs once per fixture render; only sticky specs allocate a lightweight mock wrapper.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fixture setup is synchronous except for one Promise microtask used after the synthetic click; no parallel external operations or unbounded queue is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: All state is per-fixture in-memory mock data with no cold/warm cache distinction or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence because the changed fixture code and service mocks are directly visible and do not invoke real provider, filesystem, network, IPC, database, or subprocess operations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Fixture suites may run multiple themes, but each invocation uses a tiny fixed input, so the extra array scans and mock allocation remain bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. This is test-only bounded setup work, and the screenshot markdown URL updates are inert documentation.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and every diff page. Production changes are CSS-only: one bounded sticky marker box is added, existing hierarchy-guide boxes are restyled without increasing count or event frequency, and codicon sizes are normalized. The only transitive provider IPC remains pre-existing, deduplicated, and off the paint critical path. No findings and no qualifying regression-fix learning signal.
